title: Proposal Scoring Matrix & Weighted Evaluation Rubric for Month-to-Month vs. Annual Cleaning Contracts
seoTitle: Weighted Evaluation Rubric: Month-to-Month vs. Annual Cleaning Bids
metaDescription: Use a 100-point weighted evaluation rubric for month-to-month vs. annual cleaning contracts to score $35–$65/hr labor rates and compare janitorial quotes.
excerpt: Comparing a low-ball annual janitorial bid against a flexible month-to-month proposal requires a structured 100-point scoring matrix rather than a quick look at the bottom-line monthly fee. Use this weighted evaluation rubric to benchmark labor production hours, exit protections, and compliance documentation side by side.
quickAnswer: A rigorous weighted evaluation rubric for month to month vs annual cleaning contracts assigns 100 total points across five procurement pillars: Labor Hour & Rate Realism (30 points, benchmarking against $35–$65/hr and 3,500 sq ft/hr ISSA production standards), Contract Exit & Escalation Flexibility (25 points), Periodic Floor & Dispenser Asset Care (15 points), Supervision & Quality Audit Systems (15 points), and Insurance/OSHA Compliance Verification (15 points). Any proposal scoring below 75 total points—or under 18 out of 30 on labor hour realism—should be disqualified before contract award.

blocks.text: Why Raw Monthly Price Comparisons Fail Between Month-to-Month and Annual Bids

When three building service contractors return proposals for your facility, one vendor may submit a 12-month contract at $0.075 per sq ft per visit, a second may propose a month-to-month agreement at $0.095 per sq ft per visit, and a third may offer an annual agreement at $0.085 per sq ft that bundles quarterly carpet extraction ($0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month) and paper consumables ($0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit). Comparing those three bottom-line monthly totals without normalizing contract risk, allocated labor hours, and exit flexibility leads straight to understaffed crews and mid-year change-order disputes.

Applying a weighted evaluation rubric for month to month vs annual cleaning contracts forces every bidder onto an identical 100-point scale. Instead of rewarding a vendor who simply under-allocates nightly labor hours or hides a 90-day evergreen rollover penalty behind an artificially low annual price, the scoring matrix quantifies both financial value and operational resilience.

blocks.caption: 100-Point Weighted Evaluation Rubric for Month-to-Month vs. Annual Janitorial Proposals
rows: 1. Labor Hours & Rate Realism (4.33 wks/mo)
30 Points
Discloses exact daily labor hours aligned with 3,500 sq ft/hr ISSA benchmark at $35–$65/hr; locks rate 12 mos
Flat monthly fee without hour breakdown, or M2M rate within +8% of annual benchmark
Implied production >5,200 sq ft/hr (ghost-shift pricing) or below statutory wage floor
2. Exit Flexibility & Renewal Protections
25 Points
12-mo price lock paired with 30-day termination for convenience & 15-day cure period; converts to M2M after Yr 1
True M2M with 30-day exit (no annual price lock) OR 12-mo term with for-cause-only exit
Unbreakable 12–36 mo lock-in with 60–90 day evergreen auto-renewal & >5% escalator
3. Periodic Floor Care & Hardware Stewardship
15 Points
Itemizes quarterly floor care ($0.03–$0.06/sq ft/mo) with pro-rata exit reconciliation & dispenser upkeep
Quotes floor care as ad-hoc $55–$95/hr work orders with clear per-visit pricing
Bundles unscheduled floor care with 100% early-termination clawback & zero refund right
4. Supervision Ratio & QA Inspection Cadence
15 Points
Named account manager, biweekly/monthly digital GPS photo audits, <4 hr daytime ticket response
Monthly supervisor walk-through upon client request; 24-hr complaint turnaround
No dedicated field supervisor; working cleaner acts as sole quality check
5. Insurance (COI), Bonding & OSHA Compliance
15 Points
$1M/$2M GL, statutory WC, $50k+ fidelity bond, E-Verify, site SDS binder & OSHA bloodborne certs
Standard COI provided but missing Additional Insured endorsement or dishonesty bond
1099 unclassified subcontractors or refusal to provide live Workers' Comp COI

blocks.title: Calculate Implied Production Rates Before Awarding Any Points
blocks.text: To score Category 1 accurately, divide your cleanable square footage by the vendor's proposed nightly labor hours. In a 14,000 sq ft office with mixed carpet and hard flooring (1.05x multiplier) and four multi-stall restrooms ($15–$30/visit each), a thorough nightly clean requires roughly 4.0 to 4.5 labor hours per visit (around 3,100 to 3,500 sq ft per hour). If an annual bidder quotes $1,650/month for 5x/week service (21.65 visits/mo = $76.21/visit), they can only afford 1.7 to 2.0 labor hours per night at a $38–$45/hr loaded billing rate—meaning half your building will be skipped every evening.
Scoring Hardware Compatibility and Janitorial Closet Readiness

Category 3 of the rubric (15 points) evaluates how each bidder protects your building's physical fixtures and equips their on-site crew. Under month-to-month proposals, contractors frequently resist investing in high-capacity janitorial carts or matching your building's architectural restroom dispensers, whereas an annual partner should explicitly document compatibility with your installed hardware:

items: Touchless Soap System Calibration: Verify that the bidder's consumable pricing supports installed touch-free units such as the GOJO TFX Touch-Free Foam Hand Soap Dispenser, which utilizes a 1200 mL refill cartridge (delivering 2,000+ handwashes), a skylight refill-level window, and an ADA-compliant 4-inch wall depth projection rather than swapping in cheap manual pump bottles.

Architectural Stainless Steel Dispenser Care: In Class A restrooms fitted with the Bobrick B-262 ClassicSeries Surface-Mounted Folded Towel Dispenser (satin-finish 304 stainless steel cabinet with keyed tumbler lock holding 400 C-fold or 525 multifold towels), score whether the vendor's scope includes grain-directional stainless cleaning and proper paper sizing to prevent tearing and floor litter.

On-Site Cart Organization & Security: Award full hardware readiness points to contractors who stage a dedicated Rubbermaid Commercial High-Capacity Janitorial Cleaning Cart on site—equipped with a 34-gallon zippered vinyl collection bag, three structural web shelves offering 40% more storage capacity, quiet 8-inch rear wheels, and a locking cabinet door that keeps OSHA-regulated restroom chemicals secured when rolling through open office corridors.

blocks.text: Comparing Three Real-World Bid Profiles for an 18,000 Sq Ft Office

Consider how the 100-point rubric separates three competing bids for an 18,000 sq ft corporate office requiring 5x/week weekday cleaning (21.65 visits/month, 0.90x frequency multiplier), ceramic tile restrooms (1.12x multiplier), and breakroom sanitation ($12 to $25 per visit):

items.name: Bidder A: Ultra-Low Annual Contract ($2,150/mo, Strict 12-Month Lock)
items.text: Allocates only 2.5 labor hours/night (7,200 sq ft/hr unrealistic pace) and buries a 90-day evergreen auto-renewal with no convenience exit. Scores 10/30 on Labor Realism, 5/25 on Exit Flexibility, 8/15 on Floor/Hardware, 9/15 on Supervision, and 12/15 on Compliance = 44/100 (Disqualified).

items.name: Bidder B: Pure Month-to-Month Proposal ($3,480/mo, 30-Day Notice)
items.text: Allocates 5.25 realistic labor hours/night ($0.089/sq ft/visit) with full W-2 compliance, but charges a 10% M2M risk premium, excludes quarterly floor amortization, and reserves the right to raise rates with 30 days' notice. Scores 24/30 on Labor, 18/25 on Exit/Price Stability, 11/15 on Floor/Hardware, 13/15 on Supervision, and 15/15 on Compliance = 81/100 (Qualified Runner-Up).

items.name: Bidder C: Hybrid 12-Month Price Lock with 30-Day Out Clause ($3,090/mo)
items.text: Allocates 5.25 labor hours/night ($0.079/sq ft/visit), locks pricing for 12 months, includes mutual 30-day termination for convenience after Day 60 plus a 15-day cure workflow, and provides a clear quarterly floor reconciliation ledger. Scores 29/30 on Labor, 25/25 on Exit/Price Stability, 14/15 on Floor/Hardware, 14/15 on Supervision, and 15/15 on Compliance = 97/100 (Recommended Award).

blocks.text: Pre-Award Verification Protocol for the Winning Bidder

Once your scoring committee identifies the top-scoring proposal (75+ points), execute three verification steps before issuing the notice to proceed. First, call two current commercial office references of comparable square footage (within +/- 25% of your footprint) and ask specifically whether the contractor's actual nightly staffing hours matched the proposal after Month 3. Second, verify the Certificate of Insurance directly with the issuing broker to confirm active Workers' Compensation policy dates and Additional Insured language. Third, attach your scored labor-hour table, 4.33-week visit calendar, and consumables specification sheet as Exhibit A to the final contract so sales promises become legally binding deliverables.

faqs.q: What weight should price carry when scoring month-to-month vs. annual cleaning proposals?
faqs.a: Direct pricing and labor hour realism should carry 30% of the total score (30 out of 100 points), while contract exit flexibility and rate-lock protections carry 25%. Weighting raw low price above 35% encourages bidders to under-allocate nightly labor hours below the 3,500 sq ft/hr ISSA benchmark, which invariably leads to missed restrooms and supervisor turnover within 60 days.

faqs.q: How do I score a month-to-month bid fairly against a 12-month contract in the same RFP?
faqs.a: Ask every bidder in your RFP instructions to submit two pricing columns on the bid sheet: Option 1 (Pure Month-to-Month Rate) and Option 2 (12-Month Fixed Rate with a 30-Day Termination-for-Convenience Clause after 60 days). This immediately exposes each vendor's exact short-term risk premium (typically 6% to 11%) and lets you grade all bidders on identical terms.

faqs.q: What is the minimum passing score on a 100-point janitorial evaluation rubric?
faqs.a: Set a minimum passing threshold of 75 out of 100 total points, paired with two mandatory gatekeeper thresholds: at least 18 out of 30 points in Labor Hours & Rate Realism and a full 15 out of 15 points in Insurance, Bonding & W-2 OSHA Compliance after broker verification.

faqs.q: How should we score quarterly floor care when comparing M2M and annual bids?
faqs.a: Require bidders to quote quarterly carpet extraction and VCT scrubbing ($0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/month) as a separate add-on line item rather than hiding it inside the base nightly rate. Award full points (15/15) to vendors who provide exact calendar dates for each quarterly service and a transparent pro-rata reconciliation table in the event of early termination.
